payload.title: claim-check conflates a tooling failure with a missing claim
payload.body: In tasks-claim-check.yml the guard is 'if [ -f tcli ] && node tcli check-push ...; then exit 0; fi' — so BOTH a tooling failure (install failed, or the pinned cli lacks the check-push command) AND a genuine no-claim rejection fall into the same enforce branch. With TASKS_CLAIM_ENFORCE=1 a tooling failure then prints '::error::code change without a live task claim' and exit 1 — a MISLEADING message that blocks the PR for the wrong reason (observed live: pinning CLI_VERSION to a stale 0.7.0 that predates check-push produced 'unknown command check-push' followed by the bogus no-claim error). Fix: distinguish check-push's clean reject (a known nonzero exit code / sentinel) from any other failure (missing cli, unknown command, crash). On a tooling failure, emit a distinct '::error::claim-check could not run (cli/tooling problem)' and decide fail-open vs fail-closed deliberately rather than mislabeling it a claim violation. Bonus: a tiny pre-step asserting the pinned cli exposes check-push would catch a bad pin with a clear message. Surfaced fixing the pin.
